text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended a lacklustre day with prices in the most active positions trading within a 30 cents a tonne range. Traders said that the current dearth of news from the physical market coupled with the absence of any lead from New York, closed for Independence Day, made for very quiet trading conditions. At the close near August was trading at $319.20 a tonne, down $0.70.

UNITED STATES ** - Sugar output in March 1997 amounted to 427,015 tonnes, raw value, up from 421,848 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative production in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 5.385 million tonnes against 5.517 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total production in 1995/96 reached 6.675 million tonnes, down from 7.159 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 6.916 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Sugar imports in April 1997 reached 150,845 tonnes, down from 179,820 tonnes imported in April 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (October/April) up to 1.494 million tonnes, up from 1.093 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 2.615 million tonnes against 1.557 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/April 1996/97 were Guatemala with 198,382 tonnes raws against 171,563 tonnes, Brazil with 165,133 tonnes, up from 157,657 tonnes, the Dominican Republic with 148,403 tonnes against 77,814 tonnes and the Philippines with 142,168 tonnes against nil. The largest suppliers of white sugar in October/April 1996/97 were Mexico with 21,487 tonnes against 40 tonnes and Canada with 21,177 tonnes, down from 29,483 tonnes.

Sugar exports in April 1997 amounted to 12,792 tonnes against 24,342 tonnes in April 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/April 1996/97 up to 98,449 tonnes against 193,664 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 310,341 tonnes, down from 504,854 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Jamaica with 19,319 tonnes whites against 23,986 tonnes, Haiti with 15,083 tonnes compared to 28,466 tonnes and Mexico with 14,799 tonnes against 22,746 tonnes.

JAPAN ** - Sugar imports in May 1997 amounted to 141,764 tonnes, raw value, up from 124,641 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in 1996/97 up to 1.100 million tonnes, hardly changed from last year's 1.105 million tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.681 million tonnes against 1.716 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Australia with 474,424 tonnes raws against 469,433 tonnes, Thailand with 318,309 tonnes, down from 478,376 tonnes, Cuba with 131,029 tonnes, up from 20,349 tonnes and South Africa with 114,542 tonnes compared to 129,768 tonnes.

JAMAICA ** - Sugar output in 1997/98 (November/October) is expected to reach 260,000 tonnes, raw value, up from 243,000 tonnes in 1996/97 and 237,943 tonnes in 1995/96. Molasses output is expected to rise likewise to 100,000 tonnes in 1997/98 from 93,000 tonnes in 1996/97, but down on the 101,180 tonnes achieved in 1995/96. Sugar consumption in 1997/98 is forecasted to remain flat at 120,000 tonnes.
